tone_statements.citation: Luri, Moses Dramani. 2023. Aspects of Sɩsaalɩ dialectology. International Journal of Novel Research and Development (IJNRD) 8(12): a782-a795. ISSN 2456-4184, paper ID IJNRD2312096.
tone_statements.quote: Phonologically, Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language and prominent among the functions of tone in Sɩsaalɩ is the fact that it brings about dialectal difference (example 2 &3) below: Example 2: data from Tumuluŋ dialect (2) a. bà:rà, bá:rá “roam, roamed” b. bá:rɛ́, bà:rá “go behind, went behind” […] The tone is also found to bring about grammatical difference: mark possession, mark number (example 4), mark tense (example 5) and indicate the type of sentence (statement or interrogative).
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 marked (high acute, low grave); no explicit inventory statement

tone.n_tones: 2 (H, L) as reported from earlier sources
tone.says: Introductory phonology section (1.2.3, pp. 3-5) states that Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language in which tone has lexical function (distinguishing otherwise identical words) and grammatical function (tense/aspect: present marked by low tone, past by high tone on the verb's final syllable; pronoun vs imperative distinctions), illustrated with Moran 2006: 94 examples; notes (after Rowland 1966, Blass 1975, Moran 2006) that low tone is usually left unmarked. sources.citation: Rowland, Ron. 1966. Sissala noun groups. Journal of West African Languages 3(1): 23-28.
sources.note: Sec. 2 'The phonemes' (p. 24) lists 10 vowels, 24 consonants and 'four tones: high, low, rising and falling' with their diacritics; nothing on stress or accent. Dialect: Issala of Nabugajan, 15 miles SW of Tumu.

sources.citation: Luri, Moses Dramani. 2023. Aspects of Sɩsaalɩ dialectology. International Journal of Novel Research and Development (IJNRD) 8(12): a782-a795. ISSN 2456-4184, paper ID IJNRD2312096.
sources.quote: Phonologically, Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language and prominent among the functions of tone in Sɩsaalɩ is the fact that it brings about dialectal difference (example 2 &3) below: Example 2: data from Tumuluŋ dialect (2) a. bà:rà, bá:rá “roam, roamed” b. bá:rɛ́, bà:rá “go behind, went behind” […] The tone is also found to bring about grammatical difference: mark possession, mark number (example 4), mark tense (example 5) and indicate the type of sentence (statement or interrogative).
sources.note: States that Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language; tone distinguishes dialects (verb tone patterns differ between Tumuluŋ and Bʋwaalɩ: bà:rà/bá:rá 'roam/roamed' etc.) and has grammatical functions: marks possession, number (ì 'you sg' vs í 'you pl'), tense/aspect and sentence type (statement vs interrogative). Only H (acute) and L (grave) marks are used; no inventory count, no downstep discussion; a short passage inside a dialect survey, not a tone analysis.
